2. The preemptor-petitioners sought preemption of the suit land by filing Misc. Case No. 46 of 1981 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the Court of the learned Munsif Barguna which was subsequently renumbered Misc. Case No.5 of 1986 on transfer to the Court of Assistant Judge, Betagi. The preemptor .petitioners filed the aforesaid preemption case mainly on the allegations that they were co-sharer tenants to the disputed holding by inheritance and also by purchase. But late Ismail Khan, another  co-sharer tenant to the disputed holding, transferred  the suit land to his adopted son belonging to a different family, namely, the pre emptee opposite  party No.2, Abdul Jabbar @ Abdus Satter by a  registered deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 14-2-1981. Preemptor-petitioners were not aware of this transaction at the relevant time. But he later having learnt about the same obtained the certified copy of the said Heba-bil-Ewaz and filed said pre-emption case on 11-3-1981. It is further alleged that since the said deed of Heba-bill-Ewaz speaks of payment of consideration money to the extent of Taka 400.00 it was in reality not a deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz but a deed of sale. 

 7. Mr. Md Abdus Sobhan, learned Advocate for the preemptor petitioners, strenuously argues that since consideration money case was passed the deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz in question was a Heba-bil-Ewaz for pecuniary consideration and, as such, suit land was preemptible as it was not covered by the exception mentioned under section 96(10)(C) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Advocate alternatively argues that even if the transaction in question is not considered as a Heba-bil-Ewaz for pecuniary consideration (but a Heba-bil-Ewaz without pecuniary consideration) even then the transaction is not covered by the exception under section 96(10)(c) and the suitland is not exempted from preemption inasmuch as the donee in the present case namely, Abdul Jabbar is admittedly an adopted son of the donor late Ismail Khan and he (donee) is not a relation of the donor by consanguity within three degrees. 

 'Heba-bil-ewaz' for non-pecuniary consideration is not exempted from the operation of section 26F of the Bengal Tenancy Act unless such 'hiba-bil-ewaz' is in favour of the husband or wife of the testator or the donor or of any relation, by consanguinity, within three degrees of the testator or donor."

 17. The contention of Mr Quaium that since Hiba-bil-Ewaz in the present case is made without any pecuniary consideration, even though it is made in favour of the opposite party No.2 is a stranger, the same is covered by the exception provided under section 96(10)(c) and the suit land is not liable to be preempted is not acceptable inasmuch as the decision of the said case does not support him rather it supports the decision of the case reported in 19 DLR 184. Because in the aforesaid 11 DLR 353 case it was held by Amin Ahmed CJ that a transfer in favour of a stranger by Hiba-bil-Ewaj for non-pecuniary consideration is not covered by section 26F(I)(c) of Bengal Tenancy Act which is in terms with section 96(10)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
